questions.stem: A grouped frequency table shows test scores: 0-20 (4 students), 21-40 (8), 41-60 (15), 61-80 (10), 81-100 (3). Which class interval contains the median?
questions.explanation: Total = 40 students. Median is between 20th and 21st values. Cumulative: 0-20 has 4, up to 40 has 12, up to 60 has 27. The 20th and 21st values both fall in the 41-60 class (positions 13-27).

questions.stem: Heights are grouped: 140 ≤ h < 150 (3), 150 ≤ h < 160 (12), 160 ≤ h < 170 (18), 170 ≤ h < 180 (7). What is the estimated mean height?
questions.explanation: Using midpoints: (145×3 + 155×12 + 165×18 + 175×7) / 40 = (435 + 1860 + 2970 + 1225) / 40 = 6490/40 = 162.25 cm. We must use class midpoints for grouped data, giving an estimated mean.

questions.stem: In a grouped table, the class 10 < x ≤ 20 has frequency 15. What is the class width and midpoint?
questions.explanation: Class width = upper boundary − lower boundary = 20 − 10 = 10. Midpoint = (10 + 20) / 2 = 15. The midpoint is used to estimate the mean from grouped data.

questions.stem: Weights (kg) are grouped: 50-60 (5), 60-70 (12), 70-80 (18), 80-90 (10), 90-100 (5). The class boundaries are 50 ≤ w < 60, etc. What is the modal class?
questions.explanation: The modal class is the class with the highest frequency: 70-80 with 18. For grouped data, we identify the modal class (interval), not a single value. Option (c) gives the midpoint, and (d) gives the frequency.

questions.stem: A grouped table with class intervals of equal width has: 0-10 (6), 10-20 (14), 20-30 (22), 30-40 (8). Estimate the number of values less than 25.
questions.explanation: All values below 20: 6 + 14 = 20. For 20-30 class, 25 is halfway through, so estimate 22 × 0.5 = 11 values below 25. Total estimate = 20 + 11 = 31. We assume values are evenly distributed within each class.
